system.coreAbility:
Loaded. All or nothing. The Shotgun doesn?t have Capacity
like other ranged Weapons. Instead, it is either Empty
or Loaded. At the start of each fight, the Shotgun is
Loaded: place the Shotgun token on your character
sheet with the Loaded side up. While it?s Loaded, you
can make an attack by flipping it to Empty; while it?s
Empty, you can make a Reload manoeuvre to flip it to
Loaded. You can only make attacks with the Shotgun
while it is Loaded. You may only use the sections of your
abilities matching the current state of your Weapon.
In general, effects that restore Capacity also allow you
to flip the Shotgun from Empty to Loaded.
system.outlook:
The Shotgun (or blunderbuss, or dragon, or
scattergun, or coach gun) uses a sizeable charge
to fire multiple projectiles at a target. On the upside,
the spread of shot means that accuracy is no longer a
concern - on the downside, the laborious process of
loading the ammunition leaves the bearer vulnerable to
attack once they've pulled the trigger.
It is not a new or complicated concept. Whilst
the Rifle and Pistol have made recent advances with
regards to accuracy, capacity and rate of fire, the
Shotgun has been perfectly happy to blast great clouds
of debris downrange for centuries with very little
change in its construction. It is easy to make, easy to
use, and you can fire pretty much anything out of it
and still make an impact.
It is immediate and indiscriminate violence in physical
form. It promises absolute destruction at the pull of
a trigger: an attack without patience or restraint that
sends even the fiercest foe reeling.
system.lies:
What if, the Shotgun asks, you no longer held
back? The world is a web of carefully-maintained
social constructs designed to hold our baser impulses in
check and, not coincidentally, keep power in the hands
of those who already possess it. The game is rigged
from the start, but you don't have to play it. There's an
advantage in being the wild card, and to ignore all the
restrictions and boundaries placed upon you. To do the
unthinkable. To kill and maim and ruin.
Certainly intimidation and fear have their place, but
that's not what the blood-hungry Shotgun is interested
in. It wants action. It wants to blow the world clean
in half and relish in the aftermath. It wants to break
things to prove that they can be broken. Violence is the
only form of communication that matters, and you've
got the ultimate solution to any given problem: death.
system.fears:
Death is not the ultimate solution to any problem.
The Shotgun knows this.
Those carefully-maintained social constructs can't
be torn asunder so easily. The Shotgun doesn't like to
think about what happens after the shot is fired and
the smoke clears; that it is empty, and powerless, and
open to retribution.
It hates being unloaded, and it hates not being fired.
What it desires is impossible and intoxicating: no
waiting and no need for recovery, but only an endless
instant of fury. It exists solely for that brief moment of
fire and noise and the fleeting taste of absolute power.
The lies it tells are wild and unsustainable, but to the
right person, they'll hold together long enough.
